Opress emerged from his coma and proceeded to destroy the medical droids with his new mechanical arm while Maul watched. As Opress grew agitated, Maul appeared to calm him and informed him of who they had fallen upon. He insisted that the Mandalorians would be more useful to their plans than the pirates ever would have been because the Mandalorians had honor. While Opress rejected this as a weakness, Maul stated that his plans would be better served by them and, once they had reclaimed Mandalore, they would use its resources to further their own plans, with the Death Watch under their command. Vizsla then arrived and announced that the alliance had been accepted by the Death Watch. Maul convinced Pre Vizsla they needed to recruit Black Sun so they could build an army and their resources will allow them to sustain a war without the scrutiny of the Republic, and with that, the alliance proceeded to [[Mission to Mustafar (Death Watch)|go]] to [[Mustafar]] to recruit the [[Black Sun]] into their army. They were met by [[Ziton Moj]], who brought the group to their [[Black Sun ruling council|council]]. Maul asked the council to join them, but they refused despite Maul giving them a second chance, and on Maul's orders, Savage activated his lightsaber and threw it across the table, decapitating the council and prompting Moj to form an alliance with Maul's forces. Upon returning to their camp on Zanbar, the [[Pyke Syndicate|Pykes]] also declared their allegiance to the Sith brothers. [[File:ShadowLeaders-Eminence.png|thumb|left|250px|Maul, Opress, and Pre Vizsla, leaders of the [[Shadow Collective]]]] Next, the alliance [[Mission to Nal Hutta|traveled]] to [[Nal Hutta]] to convince the [[Grand Hutt Council]] to join their group. The Hutts refused to join as they had no credits to buy their allegiance, so Maul and his forces battled the Hutts' enforcers and hired bounty hunters, with Maul fighting [[Sugi (bounty hunter)|Sugi]] and an [[anooba]] named [[Marrok (anooba)|Marrok]]. After defeating the bounty hunters and the guards, they met [[Oruba]] the Hutt, who was captured by Bo-Katan and her forces. The Hutt pleaded for help, but Maul callously ordered his brother to kill him. Before he could, Maul interrogated Oruba on the location of the other Hutts. Fearing for his life, Oruba responded with Tatooine, to which Vizsla identified as the location of [[Boba Fett's Palace|Jabba's Palace]]. Dissatisfied that the only thing Oruba could tell them was information so blatantly obvious, he gestured Opress to execute the frightened Hutt, and they headed to Jabba's Palace and [[Attack on Jabba's Palace|besieged]] it. Overwhelmed by the Death Watch, [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure|Jabba]] agreed to join the Shadow Collective. [[File:Maul_captured_at_Bahlah.png|thumb|right|250px|Maul captured by the [[Morubas Crime Family]] on [[Bahlah]]]] While searching to create his crime family,The comic [[Tales of Villainy: The Hostage]], shows Maul looking to grow his [[Shadow Collective|crime syndicate]], a journey in which he starts in the [[The Clone Wars: Season Five|Clone Wars Season Five]] episode [[Eminence (episode)|Eminence]] and ends in [[Shades of Reason]], thus "The Hostage" must take place between the two episodes, which ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' dates to [[19 BBY]] Maul and Opress sat in a [[cantina]], planning to gain the favor of the leader of the [[Morubas Crime Family]], [[Jjan]]. However, a patron at the bar overheard them and snitched on Maul to Jjan, who planned to [[poison]] Maul during his arrival. When arriving at the base, Savage [[Battle of Bahlah|led]] forces in an attempt to capture the [[Stronghold of the Morubas crime family]]. Maul entered Jjan's throne room, allowing himself to get captured in order to allow his forces to besiege the stronghold, taking the crime family's power.{{IDWAdventuresCite-2020|issue=3|story=Tales of Villainy: The Hostage}} ====Conquest of Mandalore==== {{Quote|I will use my army of crime lords to attack different targets across Sundari and sow chaos to undermine the Duchess's rule. Our gangsters will make her look too weak to maintain control. Then you and your Death Watch will capture and arrest us, bringing order where Satine's weak government could not.|Maul to Pre Vizsla|{{TCW|Shades of Reason}}}} Now with an army under his command, Maul and the Shadow Collective planned to overthrow the government of Duchess Satine on Mandalore. Their goal was to make the Duchess look weak by sending the Collective's criminal elements to [[Takeover of Mandalore|attack]] the capital city, [[Sundari]], at which time Death Watch would arrive and drive them off. Maul also anticipated and counted on Pre Vizsla and Bo-Katan betraying him, an act that he counted on as part of his own plans. After Death Watch drove the criminals away, Maul's suspicions were confirmed when he and Opress were arrested. With Maul imprisoned, Death Watch declared themselves the leaders of Mandalore. Maul suspected that there would be other political prisoners nearby, other than the deposed and imprisoned Satine, who Maul could use for his own ends. The two Sith brothers broke out of their cells and sought to find a new ally, choosing former Prime Minister [[Almec]] as a puppet; Almec had been imprisoned by the Duchess on corruption charges. Having fought his way out of prison, Maul stormed into the Mandalorian throne room, the [[Grand Salon]],''[[Collapse of the Republic]]'' and challenged Pre Vizsla to an honorable death match, knowing that the winner would gain the allegiance of Death Watch and become their new leader. After a long and spectacular duel, Maul overpowered Pre Vizsla and beheaded him with his own weapon, the [[Darksaber]] that ancient Mandalorians had stolen from the Jedi, which Maul then claimed as his own. However, Maul's victory split the Death Watch in two, with Bo-Katan and her forces refusing to pledge loyalty to Maul. The other half submitted to Maul's rule, while Almec was reinstated as Prime Minister—albeit with Maul as the true power on Mandalore. ===Ruler of Mandalore=== ====Revenge against Kenobi==== {{Quote|You can kill me, but you will never destroy me. It takes strength to resist the dark side. Only the weak embrace it.''"
"''It is more powerful than you know.''"
"''And those who oppose it are more powerful than you'll ever be. I know where you're from. I've been to your village. I know the decision to join the dark side wasn't yours; the Nightsisters made it for you.''"
"''Silence! You think you know ''me?'' It was I who languished for years thinking of nothing but ''you!'' Nothing but this moment! And now, the perfect tool for my vengeance is in front of us. I never planned on killing you, but I will make you ''share'' my pain, Kenobi.|Kenobi and Maul as Maul prepares to murder Duchess Satine Kryze in front of him|audio=ObiWan-Maul-DarkSide.flac|{{TCW|The Lawless}}}} Shortly after the coup, Maul learned that the Duchess had tried to escape from prison and transmitted a distress call to the Jedi. Having learned of Kenobi's old friendship and relationship with Kryze, Maul realized she could serve as bait for his archenemy and the perfect tool for his revenge against the Jedi Master. As Mandalore was technically neutral in the Clone Wars, Maul knew that Kenobi could not receive an official sanction from the Jedi Council for a rescue mission. As such, he predicted that Kenobi would mount his rescue alone. After Kenobi infiltrated the palace and liberated his friend, Maul and the Mandalorian forces chased the two of them all the way to Kenobi's ship, ''[[Twilight]]''. The Mandalorians fired missiles at the ship and crippled it, forcing Kenobi and Kryze to abandon ship before it was destroyed. Although dazed from the crash, Kenobi recognized Maul and Opress and attacked them, but Maul quickly disarmed him and ordered his forces to bring Kenobi and the Duchess to the palace. [[File:HoldMeObiWanKenobi-TL.png|thumb|right|250px|The Duchess dies in Kenobi's arms, as Maul claims his revenge against the Jedi Master.]] In the throne room, Maul taunted Kenobi to give in to the dark side, all the while holding Kryze in a Force grip. Kenobi angrily refused, and told Maul he had been to the Sith Lord's village on Dathomir; Kenobi further brought up Maul's past by saying that it had not been Maul's decision to join the dark side, but rather the Nightsisters forced it upon him. The comments struck a nerve, angering Maul and causing him to lash out. He reminded Kenobi that it was the Jedi Master who truly made Maul suffer for over ten years, and that it was time for Kenobi to share in his agony. At that moment, Maul activated the Darksaber and stabbed it through the Duchess's chest. Kryze died in Kenobi's arms, before Maul ordered that Kenobi be taken to the prison to contemplate his loss. Kenobi later escaped with the help of Bo-Katan, who revealed herself to be the Duchess's sister. ====Duel with Darth Sidious==== {{Quote|Remember the first and only reality of the Sith: there can only be ''two'', and ''you'' are no longer my apprentice. You have been replaced!|Darth Sidious rejects Maul's claim of Sith lordship|}} Bo-Katan and her [[Nite Owls]] [[Mandalorian Civil War (19 BBY)|fought]] Maul's [[Mandalorian super commando]]s, bringing a civil war to Mandalore. As their forces collided, Darth Sidious arrived at the royal palace, having sensed that Maul was growing stronger and had become a rival after learning of Maul's activities from Masters Kenobi and Skywalker. When Sidious arrived, Maul sensed his old master's presence and prepared to face him. Maul claimed that he had taken Mandalore and built an army in the hopes of becoming Sidious's apprentice once more, but the Dark Lord saw through Maul's deception and attacked the brothers, demonstrating his superior power through Force attacks. [[File:SidiousVsNightbrothers-TL.png|thumb|left|250px|Maul and Opress duel Darth Sidious]] After Sidious released the duo from his Force grip, all three drew their weapons and began to duel. Sidious's overwhelming prowess proved far too much for them, and he managed to stun Maul by Force-pushing him into a wall before taking on Opress alone. Maul regained consciousness just in time to see Opress be fatally impaled by Sidious's blades. Maul rushed to his brother's side, where, in his final moments, Opress expressed his regret that he had failed his brother as an apprentice. Maul watched as the Nightsister magicks that had transformed his brother leave his body, leaving Opress's original form to die by his brother's side. Sidious was amused by Maul's grief and reminded Maul that there could only be two Sith and that he had been [[Dooku|replaced]]. Enraged, Maul lit both his own lightsaber and the Darksaber, and attacked his former master. Maul held his own better than Opress, but was ultimately outclassed by the more experienced and skilled Dark Lord of the Sith and disarmed. Sidious telekinetically assaulted Maul multiple times, throwing him against walls and smashing him into the ground, severely weakening him. Maul pleaded for mercy, but Sidious riposted that in the Sith, there was no mercy and began to sadistically torture him with blasts of Force Lightning. The Sith Lord revealed he had no intention of killing his former apprentice and still had uses for Maul; he wanted to use Maul to draw Mother Talzin into the open so she could be defeated, though he did not reveal his plan to Maul. ====Capture and escape==== {{Quote|The war you have waited your entire lives to fight is upon us, my brothers. Victory or death!|Maul to his Death Watch forces|}} [[File:Stygeon_Prime_rescue.png|thumb|right|250px|Maul escapes the Spire on Stygeon Prime]] After the duel on Mandalore, Sidious took Maul as his prisoner and brought him to the remote world of [[Stygeon Prime]], where the Confederacy of Independent Systems operated the [[Spire (Stygeon Prime)|Spire]], a prison fortress in the mountains. On Almec's orders, Sidious's vessel was pursued by Maul's Death Watch forces, with the intention of rescuing their captive leader. Once he was imprisoned, Maul was subjected to torture at the hands of the Sith, as Sidious reminded Maul that he still had plans for his former apprentice. The two were interrupted by Count Dooku, whose arrival angered Maul. Dooku returned to Maul after conferring with Sidious, with orders from the Dark Lord to learn more about the Shadow Collective and the names of Maul's associates. Dooku interrogated his predecessor, electrifying him in an attempt to find the information he was seeking. Maul resisted the torture and refused to give up any information. After Dooku left, [[Rook Kast]] and [[Gar Saxon]] of Death Watch attacked the prison and rescued their captive leader. The Mandalorians blew a hole in the walls of Maul's cell, and together they rappelled down the mountain and [[Escape from the Spire|escaped]] aboard a Death Watch ship. Unknown to Maul and the Death Watch, the Sith intended for Maul to escape so he could lead them to Mother Talzin. Maul and Death Watch regrouped with more of their forces on Zanbar. After his arrival, Maul spoke to Prime Minister Almec via [[hologram]], and the Prime Minister told Maul that the prison break was repayment for when Maul released Almec from imprisonment. Once again in command of his forces, Maul reclaimed his Darksaber and promised the Mandalorians that the war they had longed for was at hand. Soon thereafter, Separatist forces under the command of [[General]] [[Grievous]] reached Zanbar. Grievous [[Battle of Zanbar|launched]] all of his forces against Death Watch, with both sides suffering heavy losses. During the battle, Maul destroyed four of Grievous's [[IG-100 MagnaGuard|MagnaGuard]] droids and attacked Grievous himself. Despite Maul's obvious power, Grievous sent him back with a kick during their blade lock. With most of his forces in ruins, Maul ordered his warriors to retreat. Grievous allowed Maul to escape, per Dooku's orders, hoping that Maul would seek out Mother Talzin for help. ====Alliance with Dooku==== {{Quote|So it is true—you are working together!''"
"''Of course. Only our hatred of you could be strong enough to unite us!|Obi-Wan Kenobi and Maul|}} [[File:Maul_Speaks_to_Talzin_Smoke.png|thumb|left|250px|Maul speaks to Mother Talzin, who appeared in a cloud of smoke.]] As Dooku predicted, Maul contacted Mother Talzin after leaving Zanbar, calling out to her through the Force for guidance. She appeared to him from afar in a cloud of smoke and he informed her of his escape from prison and defeat on Zanbar. Talzin anticipated that Sidious hoped to lure her into a trap, so she ordered Maul to go to [[Ord Mantell]], where the Black Sun had a base of operations. Once there, Talzin wanted him to gather his forces for another battle against the Separatists, this time to lure Dooku and Grievous into a trap and capture them—which Talzin believed that Sidious would not expect. Talzin herself would not go to Ord Mantell, as she knew she was a target of the Sith Lords.[[Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir 2|''Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir'' 2]] Maul arrived on Ord Mantell and conferred with his Shadow Collective allies, including Ziton Moj of Black Sun and [[Fife]] of the Pyke Syndicate. He informed them that a battle would take place against the Separatists, who were being lured to Ord Mantell thinking they could capture Maul. Despite some reservations from his allies, Maul was confident that his plan would succeed and they could trap the two Separatist leaders. Maul and his allies quickly planned their attack against the Separatists, which included luring the droid army to a specific point in the Black Sun–controlled territory so the Shadow Collective forces could attack them. As the Collective prepared for battle, a team of Nightbrother warriors, led by Brother [[Viscus]], arrived after having been sent from Dathomir by Mother Talzin to reinforce Maul's army. While Maul greeted his fellow Nightbrothers, the Separatists arrived in orbit and attacked, using their fleet to bombard the surface of Ord Mantell. Maul immediately ordered his forces to carry out their assault, while the Nightbrothers were to wait in the command center for instructions. Maul, meanwhile, made his way to Mandalorian warships, which he and Death Watch forces would use to assault the Separatist fleet in orbit. [[File:Maul_Tackles_Grievous.png|thumb|right|250px|Maul tackles General Grievous after boarding the Separatist command ship.]] Maul arrived in orbit while the Separatists began landing their troops—as well as Count Dooku—on the planet, quickly overwhelming the Shadow Collective army. Maul's ships attacked General Grievous's command vessel, before attaching itself to the hull of the Separatist ship so Maul and his forces could board and make their way to the bridge. Once there, Maul and Death Watch eliminated the battle droids defending the [[cyborg]] general, and Maul then subdued Grievous and gave him a choice: disable the signal powering the droids on the surface, or die. Grievous begrudgingly disabled the signal and was taken into custody. Dooku, who engaged and killed the Nightbrothers in battle, was captured by Shadow Collective forces on the surface, while the disabled battle droids were eliminated. After the battle, Maul contacted Mother Talzin once again to inform her of what had happened on Ord Mantell. Talzin promised Maul that, with Dooku and Grievous in custody, they would capture Sidious as well and gain their revenge against him. Maul and his forces cleared off of Ord Mantell, leaving little trace they were there, and made their way to [[Vizsla Keep 09]], a Mandalorian supply outpost. [[File:Maul_Dooku_Allies_or_Death.png|thumb|left|250px|Maul tempts Dooku to join him.]] From the outpost, Maul contacted Darth Sidious, informing him of the capture of Dooku and Grievous. Claiming that he had no further use for the two, Sidious told Maul to kill them, but the former Sith Lord had other plans. Grievous was locked in the brig, while Maul tempted Dooku to join him. They were both betrayed by Sidious, so Maul suggested that he and Dooku could be natural allies. Dooku did not believe that Sidious could be challenged, and claimed he did not think he should ally with Maul and Mother Talzin, the latter of whom once tried to kill Dooku during Grevious's invasion of [[Dathomir]]. Talzin herself appeared using Nightsister magic and told the story of how she was once an ally of Sidious, how she too was betrayed when Sidious took Maul from her, and how Sidious was already seeking to replace the Count. Neither Talzin nor Maul believed Dooku would sincerely ally with them, and simply wanted to ensure he could be taken to Dathomir.[[Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir 4|''Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir'' 4]] As they spoke, a Jedi-led Republic assault team [[Assault on Vizsla Keep 09|attacked]] the supply outpost. The Jedi, including Kenobi, [[Aayla Secura]], [[Mace Windu]], and [[Tiplee]], had tracked the Shadow Collective from Ord Mantell. With both of their lives at stake, Dooku feigned an alliance with Maul, while Grievous escaped in the chaos using an escape pod. Maul and Dooku engaged the Jedi in a lightsaber duel, which lasted until Kast shot a small missile towards the Jedi, incapacitating the Jedi and allowing Maul and Dooku to escape. ====Failure on Dathomir==== {{Quote|At last, the great deceiver comes to rescue his pawn.''"
"''I come to end this farce once and for all.|Maul and Darth Sidious|}} Having fled the outpost, Maul and his followers made their way towards Dathomir. While en route, Maul was contacted by Moj and the Pykes, who grew concerned that Maul's vendetta was causing the Shadow Collective's plans to fail. Maul assured them that they would be paid and that Sidious would die, allowing the galaxy to be controlled by the Shadow Collective. To ensure loyalty, Maul ordered Saxon to keep the Pykes and Black Sun in line. He also revealed to Dooku that he knew the Sith Lord was not an ally, and that Sidious had ordered his apprentice to feign allegiance with Maul. Once on Dathomir, Maul was greeted by Brother Viscus, who survived his fight with Dooku on Ord Mantell. The Nightbrother told Maul that they were ready for the next step of their plan, so Dooku was taken before Mother Talzin, who appeared before them in a cloud of smoke. She unleashed her magic upon the Sith Lord, using it to draw Dooku's life force so she could physically manifest herself again; Talzin's physical return required a sacrifice, and they had chosen Dooku for that purpose. They were interrupted, by an explosion ripping through the area, and the arrival of Grievous and Sidious. Sidious reminded his former apprentice that there was only one plan that mattered: Sidious'. [[File:2ndBattleDathomir-SoD-4.png|thumb|right|250px|Maul fights Grievous, while Talzin in Dooku's body fights Sidious.]] The arrival of the Dark Lord and Grievous led to a lightsaber duel, one which Talzin joined after she took control of Count Dooku's body. Talzin fought Sidious while Maul fought the cyborg general, and Sidious quickly gained the advantage over the Dathomir witch. Sidious bombarded Talzin with Force lightning, and the witch released Dooku and appeared in physical form once more. Maul, meanwhile, Force-pushed Grievous out of the opening that the explosion created. Once Sidious attacked her with a barrage of lightning, Maul pleaded with his mother to use his own life force to grow more powerful, but Talzin demanded that he retreat as she held off the Dark Lord's attacks. The witch used her powers to toss Maul from the fray and he was dragged away by Kast and another Death Watch warrior. As they fled, Maul watched as Grievous returned to fatally stab Talzin with his lightsabers. Maul fled from Dathomir, which was being [[Second Battle of Dathomir|attacked]] by the Separatists. The Shadow Collective, meanwhile, had also been defeated by Separatist forces. In Sidious's [[eye]]s, despite Maul's escape, the former Sith Lord had been eliminated as a rival to the future Sith rule of the galaxy. ====A new plan==== {{Quote|You are but one small piece moving in this mechanism which I have designed, and yet, when you falter, it jeopardizes everything.|Maul to Marg Krim|{{TCW|Together Again}}}} Maul and other parts of his loyal forces would eventually return to Mandalore, where they remained in hiding for a short time. The Pyke Syndicate and Black Sun also eventually rejoined the Shadow Collective. At some point, Maul also forged ties with the criminal organization [[Crimson Dawn]] represented by [[Dryden Vos]]. He continued to rule his operation, one part of which involved the transportation of a large shipment of [[spice]] by the Pykes. [[File:MaulThreatensKrim-TA.png|thumb|left|250px|Maul threatens to let Crimson Dawn take over Marg Krim's operation.]] The Pykes hired [[Rafa Martez]] to deliver the spice, but after a heavy ethics debate between Martez and the former Jedi Padawan [[Ahsoka Tano]], Martez's sister, [[Trace Martez|Trace]], dumped the spice into [[hyperspace]]. With no shipment to deliver, the three were taken into custody by the Pykes on [[Oba Diah]]. Shortly afterward, Maul contacted the new leader of the Pykes, [[Marg Krim]], via hologram about the lost shipment of spice. Krim attempted to assure Maul that the delay of the spice would not jeopardize his plans. Maul warned Krim of further delays, informing him that every piece of his plan was important and if one part of it faltered, the entire plan could be jeopardized. Krim attempted to defend himself by informing him of the ever-growing interference of the Republic against his shipments: one shipment that had arrived on Coruscant was raided by the Republic the week prior. Maul asked if any Jedi were involved, but Krim did not know since none of his men survived, which allowed Maul to come to the conclusion that there were. Just then, Maul noticed something hiding in the pipework surrounding where the meeting was taking place and turned to try to see what it was. After searching for a few [[Standard second|seconds]], he discovered nothing and, not realizing it was Tano, turned back towards Krim, informing him that he had other things to attend to. Maul warned him that if he caused any more delays, he would allow Crimson Dawn to take over the spice operation. With that warning, Maul ended the transmission. ====Siege of Mandalore==== {{Quote|With your help, the Jedi can stop Sidious before it's too late.''"
"''Too late for what? The Republic to fall? It already has, and you just can't see it! There is no justice, no law, no order, except for the one that will replace it!|Ahsoka Tano and Maul|}} [[File:FineArtPrints-TheUsurper.png|thumb|right|250px|Maul at the time of the Siege of Mandalore]] In a dream, Maul foresaw that [[Anakin Skywalker]] was the key to Sidious's victory as his future Sith apprentice and thus hoped to lure him and Kenobi to Mandalore: Maul hoped to rob Sidious of his prized disciple and finally achieve his revenge against Kenobi. During the final days of the Clone Wars, and two days after returning to Mandalore, Maul and his forces found themselves under [[Siege of Mandalore|siege]] by [[Bo-Katan Kryze]]'s [[Mandalore resistance|legion]] of Mandalorians and a [[332nd Division|division]] of clone troopers led by the recently promoted [[Clone Commander|Commander]] [[Rex]] and former Jedi Padawan Ahsoka Tano,{{TCW|Old Friends Not Forgotten}} instead of Skywalker and Kenobi. Maul heard from [[Almec]] and his Mandalorian forces that a Jedi was on Mandalore. Assuming that the Jedi was Kenobi, Maul instructed the Shadow Collective to lay out a trap for "Kenobi." The Shadow Collective led Ahsoka Tano and the [[Cloning|clones]] through the undercity, where they killed all of the clones, including [[Clone Captain]] [[Vaughn]]. Upon seeing that it was Tano that came to confront him, Maul told her that he was expecting Kenobi and asked why she was on Mandalore. Maul continued, telling Tano that he had hoped Kenobi would have come alongside his "loyal foal," Anakin Skywalker, to which Tano revealed that Kenobi had a more important [[Battle of Coruscant|engagement]]. When Tano asked Maul to surrender, he claimed that it would be pointless, as the Jedi Order and the Republic would soon be reduced to nothing and the galaxy would come under the control of Darth Sidious. Just then, clone forces led by Rex arrived and opened fire, forcing Maul and his Mandalorian forces to flee. During the ensuing combat, Maul captured and interrogated [[Advanced Recon Commando|ARC trooper]] [[Jesse]] about Ahsoka's history, but Jesse refused to tell him anything. Maul ordered [[Gar Saxon]] to assassinate the captured Almec before he could reveal any vital information to the enemy. Afterward, he focused again on Jesse and eventually managed to make him reveal everything he wanted to know using a [[Mind probe (Force power)|mind probe]]. [[File:SyndicateLeadersGoHide-TPA.png|thumb|left|275px|Maul orders Ziton Moj, Marg Krim, and Dryden Vos to go into hiding.]] Later, Maul was speaking with Shadow Collective leaders [[Marg Krim]] of the Pyke Syndicate, [[Ziton Moj]] of the Black Sun, and Dryden Vos of Crimson Dawn, ordering them to go into hiding, when Saxon returned to report the success of his mission. Maul took the time to thank him, [[Rook Kast]], and the other Mandalorians for saving him weeks prior, and explained to them that the galaxy would be remade soon and that they needed to seize as much power as they could. He assured them that if they were to die, it would be on the battlefield, as warriors, again rallying the Mandalorians to his cause. Sometime later, Maul returned to the throne room when Ahsoka Tano, Bo-Katan, and Rex entered. Bo-Katan attempted to attack him, but Maul effortlessly waved away her blaster bolts and subdued her before handing Jesse back to them as a show of "good faith." After Tano told Bo-Katan and Rex to leave, Maul was left alone with her. As the battle outside was raging on, Maul began talking in a calm manner to Ahsoka, reminding her of the hypocrisy of the Jedi Order, which caused her to leave, and that they were both tools used by a greater power. Maul then told her again that what she called justice would soon be changed along with the entire galaxy, revealing that he was talking about Sidious. Ahsoka suggested that Maul help the Jedi stop Sidious before this would happen, only for Maul to insist that it was already too late, as the Republic was too corrupted to be saved and the Jedi couldn't possibly stop Sidious. Maul then asked Ahsoka to join him, suggesting that together they could defeat Sidious. After a long moment of consideration, Ahsoka agreed on the condition that Maul answer one question: what did he want with Skywalker. He stated that he was the key to everything, to destruction, and that he had a vision which revealed that Sidious sought to make Skywalker his new apprentice. When Ahsoka accused him of lying, Maul explained that he had engineered the conflict on Mandalore to lure out Kenobi and Skywalker, so that he could kill the latter before he would turn to the Dark Side. Hearing this, Ahsoka changed her mind and ignited her lightsabers, stating that she knew Skywalker and he could never turn. Angered by the rejection, Maul stated that Ahsoka needed one more lesson and activated his own lightsaber. [[File:MaulAhsokaClash-TPA.png|thumb|right|250px|After his offer to work together to destroy Sidious was denied, Maul engaged Ahsoka in a fierce duel that began in the throne room.]] The two [[Force-Sensitive Outcast]]s then engaged in a fierce duel, during which Ahsoka proved to be a very tough opponent for Maul, despite the latter being stronger and far more experienced than her. Maul managed to disarm Ahsoka of her main saber, though she quickly retrieved it with the Force. Ahsoka then taunted Maul, stating he was lucky Anakin had not shown up. Maul compared this to Kenobi's arrogance. The two continued fighting and briefly engaged in a saber lock, with Maul gaining the upper hand, though he was caught by surprise by Ahsoka, who managed to kick him outside through a glass window. ====Caught and released==== {{Quote|Now, if you will follow my lead—''"
"''You don't understand. I'm not here to team up with you. I need a diversion, and you're it. Now go cause some chaos. It's what you're good at.''"
"''Uh, care to give me a fighting chance?''"
"''I'm not rooting for you. Now get going.|Maul and Ahsoka Tano, after she freed him|audio=NotRootingForYou-Shattered.flac|{{TCW|Shattered}}}} [[File:OneFinalTime.png|left|thumb|300x300px|After disarming Ahsoka, Maul gave her one last chance to join him or die.]] Outside, Ahsoka chased Maul to the top of a building. As his Mandalorian forces were being overrun, Saxon contacted Maul asking for reinforcements, but he abandoned him, saying that a ship would soon be arriving to pick him up. Saxon and his forces were outnumbered by clone troopers and forced to surrender shortly afterward. As Maul reached the top of the building, Ahsoka caught up with him and the two resumed their duel, before Maul's ship arrived to pick him up. Ahsoka stopped him from escaping, only for Maul to disarm her of both her lightsabers and slash the beam she was standing on. With Tano cornered, Maul gave her one last chance to join him, but she refused, causing him to slash at her angrily. Dodging his strikes, Tano grabbed Maul's saber and tripped him over the edge of the beam, though she saved him from falling to his death with the Force. Preferring to die rather than be captured, Maul told Ahsoka to let him fall, but she refused, just as three [[Low Altitude Assault Transport/infantry|LAAT gunships]] arrived. Maul furiously told Ahsoka she had no idea what she had just done and that they were all going to die soon, before being stunned and taken into custody. The Shadow Collective would collapse after Maul's defeat at Mandalore.{{SWKidsYouTube|series=Star Wars: Much to Learn|text=Pyke Syndicate|video=KDGOFRHM2f4|nolive=1}} Maul was subsequently imprisoned within a [[Mandalorian vault]] designed to restrain Force-users and placed aboard the [[Venator-class Star Destroyer|''Venator''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Tribunal]]''''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Character Encyclopedia - Join the Battle!]]'' commanded by Ahsoka, who was told by the [[Jedi High Council]] to bring him to Coruscant so that he could stand trial for his crimes. [[Skirmish aboard the Tribunal|En route]] to Coruscant however, Palpatine (who had revealed himself as Darth Sidious) initiated [[Order 66]], causing Rex and the rest of Ahsoka's clone troopers to turn on her. Maul sensed these events while in his captivity, before a pair of clones arrived to execute him, having received a different order from Sidious, who wanted to be rid of his former apprentice once and for all. [[File:UrsaBoKatanTransportMaul-Shattered.png|thumb|right|300px|Maul, restrained within a Mandalorian vault, being escorted by Bo-Katan Kryze, Ursa Wren and other Nite Owls.]] Before the clones could shoot the renegade Sith Lord, Ahsoka knocked them out and subsequently freed Maul from his restraints. He expressed his surprise that Tano had survived, but she threatened him with her lightsabers and demanded to know if he was behind the events, which the former Sith denied. She then revealed that the clones had turned against her and Maul laughed at the "brilliance" of Sidious' plan to use the Jedi's army to destroy them, much to her disgust. Maul went on to explain that despite being Sidious's apprentice, he was unaware of the plan's finer details. He then proposed a team-up with the former Jedi Padawan, but she harshly rejected his offer and told him he was merely a distraction to cause some chaos, refusing to lend him one of her weapons to aid in his escape. Despite being unarmed, Maul, using the Force to rip panels from the walls, tore a path of destruction through the ship, slaughtering every clone trooper in his way. When a group of clones attempted to seal themselves off from him, he used the Force to pull one of the troopers' arms through the closing [[blast door]], severing it and providing Maul with an active [[wrist comm]] connection to the clones' radio chatter.{{TCW|Victory and Death}} Maul then made his way to the [[hyperdrive]] room, still using his stolen wrist comm to listen in on the clones. Two troopers then showed up and aimed their guns at him, but he effortlessly lifted them into the air and choked them. Entering the hyperdrive room, Maul quickly dispatched of all the clones using the Force, and tore the control console away before pulling the hyperdrive generators down, causing the vessel to drop out of lightspeed over a [[Unidentified moon|moon]], where it became caught in its gravity well. As the ship began falling out of the sky and onto the moon's surface, Maul made his way to the [[hangar]] and began running towards a [[Nu-class attack/transport shuttle|''Nu''-class attack/transport shuttle]]. Ahsoka saw him and gave chase, but Maul attacked her with the Force and said that he was only causing chaos as she wanted. Enraged, Ahsoka nearly killed him with a swipe from her lightsabers, but he retaliated by pushing her into a pit, though she was saved by the [[astromech droid]] [[RG-G1]]. Maul then tried to take off in the shuttle and, though Ahsoka attempted to stop him again and grabbed the shuttle using the Force, she was ultimately forced to let him go when both [[R7-A7]] and Rex (who had had his [[behavioral modification biochip]] removed by Ahsoka) were shot by clone troopers, allowing Maul to escape into hyperspace,{{TCW|Victory and Death}} planning to rebuild his empire. [[File:MaulDestroysHyperdrive-VaD.png|thumb|left|300px|Maul destroys the hyperdrive with the Force]] In the [[Klegger Corp Mining Facility|Mustafarian mining facility]] on Mustafar, Obi-Wan Kenobi and Anakin Skywalker [[Duel on Mustafar|dueled each other]] and made their way into the [[Separatist Council war room|war room]] and momentarily into a nearby [[Separatist Council Conference Room|conference room]]. During the duel with his former apprentice, feeling his former friend's focused hatred was horrifying, as Kenobi had felt it from Maul, Dooku, Opress, and Ventress.{{EncyclopediaCite|The End of the Clone Wars}} ===Age of the Empire=== ====Forging a new path==== {{Quote|You were part of an order poised to serve the Republic. You don't realize the fragility of these institutions until they're ripped away. I felt certain of my destiny once as well, but...that was before my master cast me aside. I had to find my own way. My brother was murdered. My mother was murdered. All by the same enemy who destroyed your order.|Maul to Devon Izara|{{MSL|Chapter 3: Whispers in the Unknown}}}} As Maul had foreseen, Anakin Skywalker did indeed fall to the dark side, becoming Sidious' next apprentice and taking on the name Darth Vader. With his new student at his side, Sidious established the [[Galactic Empire]] and enacted the [[Great Jedi Purge]], the next step in his grand plan.{{Film|III}} Vader and the [[Jedi hunter|Jedi-hunting]] [[Inquisitorius]] were set loose to eradicate the Order that Maul had once wished to topple.[[Darth Vader (2017) 14|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 14]] Nearly losing his life to the final machinations of his former master's grand scheme, Order 66, and having been deprived of his planet of operations on Mandalore, Maul found himself at a critical juncture in his plans for power and vengeance. Now, having failed his race against the clock to carve out a corner of the galaxy to build a stable influence, the former Darth Maul now saw the end results of the Grand Plan he had once been a tool of. Far from what he had envisioned, the burgeoning Empire that had evolved from the bones of the decaying Republic did manage to rid the galaxy's prime source of Maul's hatred, the Jedi Order. Thousands of years of peace, civilisation, and stability under the guidance and protection of the institution representing the Light Side had been uprooted by the very system that it was serving. In spite of this, Maul was perturbed by the replacement of a cold, sterile, bureaucratic entity which demanded order through threat of force, and a galaxy filled with corruption and unpredictable chaos that even Maul found difficulty navigating.{{MSL|Chapter 1: The Dark Revenge}} For all his resentment and immense hatred for the Jedi, Maul ironically found himself wishing for their continued presence rather than near annihilation at this time. The Clone Wars, which had weakened much of the galaxy and distracted the attention of the Jedi to allow Maul the opportunity for building his own power base, one which he hoped would grow enough in the shadows of the underworld to rival Sidious' might by the end of the war. Unfortunately, despite abandoning his former destiny as the enforcer of Sidious' will, the ex-Sith still used the methods of his brutal teachings in the Dark Side: puppetry, fear, hatred and domination. His greed and ambition exposed Maul too early, and with the Siege of Mandalore, much of the Shadow Collective's unity was severed once its head was forced into hiding. Seeking to access the allegiance of his most powerful syndicates, Maul travelled to Oba Diah to ask for assistance from the Pykes. However, now that the feared Zabrak had been defeated twice on Mandalore and found himself weakened and alone, the Pyke leader, Marg Krim, desired to take control back and tried instead to have Maul killed, betraying his own boss. [[Attempt to assassinate Maul|The assassination attempt]] would fail and Maul escaped and was left with a desire for revenge against the treasonous Krim..{{MSL|Chapter 4: Pride and Vengeance}} [[File:BarrsFiles-2017DarthVader14.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Barr gathered information about Maul.]] Following the outbreak of the Jedi Purge, Maul became a subject of interest to the renegade Padawan [[Ferren Barr]], who kept a file on the former Sith Lord within the archives of [[Endee]], an [[R1-series astromech droid]] under his possession. Barr had gathered information on both Maul as well as several other subjects, hoping to better understand how the Jedi met their downfall so quickly at the hands of the Sith. During the [[Invasion of Mon Cala]][[Darth Vader (2017) 16|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 16]] in [[18 BBY]],According to ''[[Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition]]'', the occupation of Mon Cala took place a year into the [[Darth Sidious|Emperor's]] rule. Since ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' dates the beginning of Imperial rule to [[19 BBY]], the occupation of Mon Cala took place in [[18 BBY]]. Barr and [[Ferren Barr's disciples|his disciples]] were discovered by Vader. The Padawan had Endee upload a backup of the archive to a [[datacard]] before instructing the droid to [[Self-destruct mechanism|self-destruct]]. Barr himself died in combat with Vader soon after.[[Darth Vader (2017) 17|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 17]] ====Taking over Janix==== [[File:MakingAGetaway-TheDarkRevenge.png|thumb|left|240px|On Janix, Maul began to rebuild the Shadow Collective by killing Vario and Deemis before moving to the other syndicates like the Black Sun, Crimson Dawn, and Pyke Syndicate.]] First, Maul needed to find a new planet out of Imperial surveillance in order to enact his revenge against Marg Krim and establish a hideout for his loyal remnants. The [[Mid Rim Territories|Mid Rim]] world of [[Janix]] proved the perfect place, a populous and peaceful planet with smaller syndicates like the [[Aleena]] crime lord, [[Looti Vario]], who scheduled [[spice]] [[Smuggler|smuggling]] with the Pyke Syndicate. The second phase of the plan was to instigate looting and destruction on the turf of Vario's prime rival, [[Head Boss]] [[Nico Deemis]]. Ordering his chief lieutenant, Rook Kast, to steal Deemis' [[credit brick]]s and the main [[Unidentified bank supervisor droid|protocol droid]] overseeing Deemis' bank, Maul created the perfect implication of heated aggression between the two small crime leaders. Throughout the months on Janix, Maul had been receiving visions of an unknown Force-sensitive being, a Jedi he surmised, which he would turn into an apprentice to be used as a weapon in his grander plans for the future. During his ordered robbery of Deemis, Maul's soldiers drew the attention of the local authorities responsible for keeping things peaceful in Janix city, the [[Tactical Defense Force]]. With the main [[bank transport]] getting damaged, the remnant soldiers drew the cops to the top of a building where from their [[shuttle]], Maul revealed himself in a cloak and ignited his lightsaber, killing all law enforcement there; [[police droid]]s and Officer [[Pak (Tactical Defense Force)|Pak]], before vanishing. After the successful robbery of Deemis' bank, Maul was sitting in quiet meditation when approached by Rook. She inquired about his visions, to which Maul noted that Janix had been calling to him through the Force as well, since he could sense his future apprentice more clearly on the planet. When questioned about why they waste time with low-level threats like Deemis and Vario, Maul planned to use them to get to the bigger fish, the Pykes. Perturbed by Deemis' upholding of the truce between him and Vario, Maul decided they needed to send a more direct message in order to set the two syndicates into war. The end result saw Vario kill Deemis and get captured by the police, an outcome not suitable for Maul. [[File:MaulStance-MaulShadowLord.png|thumb|right|270px|Maul ready to attack the Tactical Defense Force]] The rogue Sith noted nothing would save his enemies from revenge, whether it be a cell or protection. He also sensed something else drawing him to the Tactical Defense Force's prison. Maul knew he could not risk Vario in the custody of the planet's authorities if he wanted to keep away from the Empire's eyes; therefore, he took with him his Dathomirian soldiers and [[Spybot]] to infiltrate and kidnap Vario personally. From Spybot's cutting the power and cameras of the entire building, Maul, flanked by his two Dathomirian soldiers, cut through dozens of guards and droids to reach the cell holding Vario. When face-to-face with the small traitor, Maul pointed his lightsaber next to him, moving the blade closer and closer to Vario's head. When given an offer to get to the Pyke leader Krim, Maul took him alive, knowing the cowering Aleena would prove useful in drawing out the major players of his betrayal. Ordering the Nightbrothers [[Icarus]] and [[Scorn]] to take Vario alive, the two Zabraks took him. Noting a strange sensation in the Force, Maul turned to the cell behind him to see a young, pink female Twi'lek and recognised her connection in the Force, knowing he saw the Jedi from his visions. Opening the cell door, Maul approached her as the Twi'lek uttered his name in fear. Taking her with him, Maul and his forces escaped through a vertical hatch via a long ladder, with the Zabrak at the top point deflecting incoming fire from the swarming law enforcers, while Icarus used a [[chaingun]] to fire back. The Jedi Padawan fought off one of Maul's guards and tried to flee, but was knocked out by a [[stun]] blast from Spybot. Falling down to a lower platform, Maul and his forces escaped through a door and blasted it shut from their end. A landspeeder and the stolen bank transport arrived to help them escape back to base, but their departure was intercepted by many [[Tactical Defense Force cruiser]]s. To their surprise, suddenly the landspeeder carrying Vario got damaged and crashed as the bank transport carrying Maul and the Padawan crashed too. Entering outside the bank transport, a cloaked Maul saw the source of the crash, a [[Eeko-Dio Daki|small hooded Mosyk male]] with a cane. Yet in the Force, Maul felt the real being, a Jedi Master, the one who taught the Twi'lek he had abducted. Not bothering with the Padawan trying to reunite with her master, Maul walked straight to the [[Mosyk]] Jedi to end his attacker, only to be surrounded by several speeders of law enforcement. Deciding to escape was their most prudent path, Maul flexed his finger slightly to sever the cables supporting an overhead bridge, which cracked the stone in two, endangering the pedestrians above. Knowing the Jedi Master's weak code to always save civilians, Maul created a distraction, which made the Jedi struggle to hold the bridge stable within the Force as the cops tried to help the innocents. They made their escape as his enemies tried to stabilise the bridge.{{MSL|Chapter 2: Sinister Schemes}} Returned to their hideout, Maul had the Twi'lek brought before him and commanded his Mandalorians to heal her hurt wrist, whilst he questioned her name. Only getting resistance from the Padawan, Maul tried to be cordial with her, desiring to probe the young Jedi's moral code to a broader view of the Force. When she refused him, Maul locked her and Vario in two large cells locked by huge pressurised doors. Staring into the defiant Jedi's eyes, Maul explained to her the life of indoctrination she had been brought up in to be failing her, urging her to break free. Meanwhile, Maul used Vario's intel on the Pyke shipment routines to work with the crime lord's syndicate to get a location on the next arrival of spice. A moment later, Maul returned the imprisoned Jedi to challenge her viewpoints and beliefs, a more subtle manipulation to test his possible future apprentice's resolve. Desiring to speak in truths, Maul asked for the young Jedi's feelings of being a guardian of peace and justice during an era where none existed. Nonetheless, the Twi'lek understood his attempts at turning her and showed she knew his nature and false conceit as a reasonable, benevolent being. Having experienced for himself the grey between the factions of the Light Side and the Dark Side during the war, Maul merely presented that her shrewd perception of him as a villain was a naive point of view in a complicated galaxy. Asking her again what it would take to convince her, the Twi'lek said to release her. Not amused by her continuing lack of cooperation, the rogue Sith coldly stated for her to free herself by any means, forcing her to forge an escape alone. Sowing the seeds of doubt and new possibilities in her mind, Maul left her when Rook Kast confirmed the incoming Pyke spice arrival. [[File:KastSuperCommandos-SinisterSchemes.jpg|thumb|left|270px|Kidnapping Vario, Maul caused a disruption to Krim's network on Janix.]] Once the ''[[Hex (Kom'rk-class)|Hex]]'' landed on one of Janix's moon, Maul himself entered the [[Unidentified starship (Pyke Syndicate)|Pyke cruiser]] alone, thanks to Spybot controlling the [[Turbolift|cargolifts]], and cut through all the Pykes inside. As Maul kills the crew, Kast and four Mandalorians steal the Pyke's money. Cornering the captain at the cockpit, Maul deflects his blaster fire before Force pushing him against the controls and using the Force to hurl [[Unidentified Pyke captain|their captain]] into the roof. When taunted that his victory would be momentary like his former underworld empire, Maul sarcastically agrees before let go and cut down the Pyke captain in half. This would provide a push for Marg Krim to contact Vario directly for answers when one of his shipments got attacked. Four of Krim's enforcers interrogated [[Vario's syndicate]] and killed one of his smugglers to send a message but Maul sent Kast and his forces to kill the Pykes. After returning to check on the prisoners, Maul was disappointed to see the Twi'lek still unwilling to try to break away from her Jedi restraints. Commanding his voice, Maul implored her directly to stop wasting time pretending and accept the realities of the galaxy, a place where results only happen to those with the will to shape it. Leaving her with the final verbal push, Maul sat down in his chambers to await the Jedi, if she proved willing. Some moments later, Maul welcomed her to sit with him and offered her some [[Cassius tea]] as a show of faith. The giant door locked behind them, trapping the two former followers of Force institutions. Trying once more to get a name, Maul acted in a harmless position to lower the Jedi's guard, encouraging her to view a more nuanced perception of him beyond the monster she had been told by the Jedi Order. Instead of subjugating her through torture or lying, as were the tools of his master, the war-weary Dark Sider presented a less dogmatic understanding of character than her accusations of a murderer, acknowledging the truth behind the allegation, but justified acts of violence for survival as something she could understand herself post Order 66. Just as he further instilled doubts into her binary separation of the two of them by relating to the vulnerability of the institutions they served, invisible until they are cast outside of them. Sharing how he, too, had been as assured of destiny as her once, and in return losing his brother and mother to the same adversary, who destroyed the millennia-old Jedi Order. Again, he challenged her whether they were still so entirely different. In retaliation, the Twi'lek took Maul's lightsaber, which had been lying in front of her during the conversation, declaring her plans to leave. Finally, Maul became amused by the Jedi pushing through her restraints and demonstrating a will to fight her way out, noting he could work with that much to her chagrin before extinguishing the lights in the room. Maneuvering through the shadows silently, Maul taunted the frightened Padawan that even while wielding a lightsaber, her instincts were to flee. She answered that to challenge him would be foolish, to which Maul stated that she proved no fool, but untested. Feigning her to acknowledge the theft and thirst of her destiny, Maul appeared from the shadows occasionally, goading her into feeding her hatred and frustrations and trying to kill him. After a long series of probing her thoughts, Maul offered her a choice: unlock her full potential under his teachings and help him successfully vanquish their common foe. Pressuring her to enact vengeance in memory of her Order's responsibilities, the Twi'lek, though visibly shaken, still held fast and climbed to escape. Intercepting her on a catwalk before the door, Maul expressed disappointment that she didn't really think he would willingly allow her to get away. His earlier mental attacks had worked as the young Jedi challenged him directly, showing no more fear of fighting him. Casually walking to her, Maul merely noted her bravery was not at issue, but simply her weakness. Holding one arm behind him, Maul ignited his original half of the double-bladed weapon and effortlessly engaged in Makashi flourishes to meet her desperate offensive. Forcing her to retreat as easily as he accused her of failure as a surviving Jedi, Maul decimated her remaining composure as her attacks got wilder and more aggressive. Parrying all her attacks and tripping her off her feet, Maul dominated the duel to show their gap in power. Pointing the end of his lightsaber at her like a condemning finger, he at long last broke through her hesitation by calling her life a ruin, as the Twi'lek used the Dark Side to [[force push]] Maul slightly away, placing herself towards the door. As she ran, Maul summoned his other lightsaber from her grip and called her by her name, Devon Izara, showing he knew her alias all along, as a final demonstration of his superior power over her. Thus, Maul willingly allowed her to leave, having successfully broken through her idealism. ====Punishing Krim and fighting the police and Jedi==== {{Quote|I was alone and weak after the tragic events on Mandalore. And I came here to you, my old ally, seeking safe haven. But you tried to kill me. You failed.|Maul, to Krim's corpse|}} [[File:Maul_laments_Krims_betrayal.png|thumb|right|240px|Using Vario, Maul killed Krim for his betrayal and took back control over the Pyke Syndicate.]] For his next move, Maul made Vario lie to Marg Krim in a holo-transmission by promising to deliver the lost spice to Oba Diah. This allowed Maul to easily get right onto Krim's own home to deal with the traitor. Once the [[Lau cargo ship]] landed, Maul lended one of his lightsabers and cloak to Icarus, Maul orchestrated a ruse in which Vario stunned the decoy Maul, who attacked the Pykes in order to get a personal audience with Marg Krim at the throne room. When Vario was brought before Krim, Maul made his way to the throne room and revealed his presence to Krim. Calling back his lightsaber with the Force from the Pyke leader's hands, he simultaneously spun it across Krim's chest, killing him immediately. He then combined both lightsabers to a double bladed weapon and quickly eliminated all but three of the Pyke soldiers. Dropping their weapons in defeat, Maul stood over the dead Pyke leader to condemn Krim for denying him asylum after Mandalore fell, even more for failing to kill him. Demonstrating this, the end result of all who dared to betray him, the remaining guards kneeled in submission. Calling the [[Captain of the Guard]], [[Kalt]], Maul placed the cowering Pyke in charge of the crime syndicate, but adhering to his orders. With this, Maul had effectively dealt with one of the two major factions that had betrayed him, having reclaimed control of the powerful Pyke Syndicate, he could now move onto other treasonous factions, such as Crimson Dawn. The next move was one he had planned for by releasing Izara, knowing she and her master would not resist the opportunity to inform the Tactical Defense Corps of his base location. Predictably, he was proven right as more than thirty law enforcement officers led by the pestering Captain Lawson entered his lair by nightfall. Giving Vario a [[holoprojector]], Maul presented himself via [[hologram]] to talk directly to the cop that had been chasing him the last few days. Complementing Lawson as a man of integrity and intellect for not alerting the Empire, Maul stated their common goal of keeping Imperial presence of Janix. Offering a deal, he gave a promise that he would keep his interests and operations away from Janix's population and give protection to the authorities, if he was allowed to operate in the shadows of the planet uninterrupted and without the Empire there. To his disappointed presumption, Lawson refused, though Maul admired his duty to honor. He then ordered his forces to kill all of them and watched the escalated firestorm beneath him, whilst, using the Force to crush Lawson's [[probe droid]]. The renegade Sith lord's second expectation appeared before him as Izara had returned with her master Daki to challenge him. Chuckling at the old Jedi's tiring philosophy of servitude to beings beneath them, Maul basked in flouting the failures of Jedi passivism by the humiliating conditions the two fugitives found themselves in, begging for scraps, booted down by the Republic they swore to serve  and failing to seize power waiting there. Reinforcing his own twisted perception of power and destiny, Maul showed his still dominant Sith beliefs by determining the Jedi's failure as a result of answering to the will of the Force, rather than controlling it by their own will to shape the galaxy. Finished with the futile debate, Maul ignited his double-bladed lightsaber as a signal to settle their dispute by combat. The Jedi Master and Padawan ignited their lylat lightsabers in coordination, and the three Force-sensitive fugitives engaged in a duel. Proving himself more than a match against them, the two Jedi failed to meet a real challenge like his glorious battle against Kenobi and Qui-Gon Jinn on Naboo, letting Maul decide the balance of the exchanges, separating Padawan and Master from each other. Individually, they were no match against him, but combined, they helped each other avoid getting overwhelmed by him. Nevertheless, Maul handled them together as well as one by one, using one end of his blade to parry Izara and the other to meet Daki. After kicking the old Jedi against some stairs, Maul force pushed away Izara and reengaged with Daki. To his surprise, Daki quickly retaliated with a swift kick to Maul's cybernetic knee joint, causing some slight malfunction in the mechanism and greatly angering the Zabrak. [[File:Devon_duels_Maul.png|thumb|left|280px|Maul defeated Devon and Daki.]] Taking the offensive, Maul unleashed rapid strikes against the retreating Master as they ascended the stairs, the Sith's blades melting through the support beams. After a short sabre lock, Maul powered through and delivered a hefty kick which knocked Daki onto a cradle beneath, leaving the [[Mosyk]] in pain and without a lightsaber. Holding his weapon overhead, Maul struck down a fatal blow, but was blocked at the last second by a recovered Izara, who positioned herself before her master. Congratulating her for aiding her master, Maul disengaged as his forces started to retreat and pointed his blade at the defeated pair. Smiling from Izara's tenacity and dedication, Maul disappeared. Running through the tunnels behind his soldiers, Maul stopped from his damaged right cybernetic leg and took the opportunity to collapse rubble and pipes from the roof to block their exit from pursuers. Hearing Rook Kast state that something had gone wrong, Maul already knew the truth to that statement: the Empire had arrived on Janix. ====Hunted by the Empire==== {{Quote|I offer not only to train you to reach your full potential, but also because I need your help...to fight a common enemy."
"The Empire?"
"The Jedi were once revered protectors of the Galaxy, but now they are considered traitors. Oh, how that must bite, to live as a fugitive. Hand to mouth. Have you ever encountered one of the Jedi hunters? Are you even prepared?"
"I'll take my chances.|Maul and [[Devon Izara]]|}} [[File:Operations_on_Janix.jpg|thumb|right|280px|The Empire arrived on Janix after hearing Maul's pressence.]] Having been exposed to the Empire, Maul's previously low-cover operations on Janix came to a complete halt as the rogue Force user abandoned the safehouse and travelled further down to the lower levels of Janix city. The cityscape above had been eclipsed by the shadow of an Imperial Star Destroyer, a new formidable battle cruiser that helped hinder traffic and locked down all space ports for orbital travel. Routine checks and massive troop displacement had made Janix into a quarantined zone, and Kast urged her lord to leave the planet while they still could. His lieutenant stated Izara tried to kill him, therefore proving unwilling to join them. Yet, Maul only respected the young woman's tenacity for challenging him, a desirable trait in an apprentice. Moreover, he knew that his temptations of Izara's character had been fruitful in cracking her Jedi lens, and with the arrival of the Empire, the Padawan and Master were equally trapped, which would force them to desperation. Thus, if he timed his actions, Maul could provide help to the young Twi'lek where her master would fail, especially since the Zabrak knew of the [[Jedi hunter]]s in the Empire's ranks: the [[Inquisitorius]].{{MSL|Chapter 5: Inquisition}} The blow delivered to his cybernetic knee by Master Daki continued to malfunction, so the Nightbrother Icarus made some repairs and tended to the mechanisms to fix the damage. Interrupted again by Kast, a beleaguered Maul demanded the information, which she noted that there had been a scuffle above and that the Jedi pair had encountered TK troops above. Deducing the Inquisitor now to be tracking and soon fighting the fugitive Jedi, Maul started training his saber techniques after his leg was fixed. His training stopped when Rook Kast summoned him to see footage that Spybot had caught. The Inquisitor had been in their warehouse investigating. [[File:MarrokFightingMaul.png|thumb|left|240px|Maul dueling the First Brother.]] Keeping an eye on the Imperial feeds through Spybot, Maul later received information about troops engaged in combat with runaway targets in Sector 9. Concluding the opportunity to reveal himself to be perfect, the shadow lord walked to offer assistance to Davon, which, predictably, did not sit well with Kast. Justifying that the strong grow only when forged through dire circumstances, he would willingly ally himself with Izera if she proved her worth and resilience against the Inquisitor. Getting her location via Spybot's intel, Maul boarded a speeding [[hovertrain]] as watched as Izara fought valiantly against the armoured Inquisitor. As the masked fiend demanded the location of the target Sith from Izara, Maul fittingly made his presence known and jumped mid air with his ignited lightsaber and struck the Inquisitor back. Putting himself between the Padawan and her hunter, Maul engaged the Imperial in a swift duel along the tunneling train, landing blow and parries, landing a kick on the Inquisitor who returned with a blow to Maul's head. As they fought on, Izara joined Maul, and together they exchanged blows with [[Marrok|First Brother]], forcing him back towards the train.{{MSL|Chapter 6: Night of the Hunted}} At one point, Maul blocked a strike aimed at Izara as she was down, submitting his presence to her as a protector. Parried away for a moment, the First Brother separated the two and reengaged Maul, while using a Force Push to keep the Padawan away. The next attack from Maul got blocked by the First Brother, who grabbed the lightsaber arm, and Maul answered in kind, holding the opponent's lightsaber from his head. Not knowing he was facing the end of a double-sided lightsaber, Maul barely moved away as the second blade ignited centimeters from his face, forcing Maul to break off the deadlock and free his saber arm. The First Brother took the break off to start spinning his double-sided weapon at lightning pace through a hinge mechanism. Unintimidated by the move, Maul ignited the other end of his own lightsaber and manually spun it around himself to prove the difference in skill. Quickly, the two Dark Siders fought again, both with their unorthodox red lightsabers, evenly until Maul threw his weapon at the Inquisitor, making the opponent jump over to the [[train]] cart behind. Standing side by side with Izara, the fight ended when she severed the connection clamp between the two train carts with her lightsaber, leaving the hunter behind as their train portion continued speeding through the tunnel. With their common foe out of sight, the Jedi turned her lightsaber against Maul with a determined look to fight him. Undeterred, Maul merely extinguished his weapon and lowered the Twi'lek's sense of threat. Crossing his arms, the Nightbrother verbalised the truth to the insecure Padawan what he had already told her: he was not her enemy, the Empire was. Abandoning the train, the trio made their way on foot through the cascading tunnel to reach Maul´s hideout, with the Sith taking the lead. Listening to his two cautious companions debating whether to follow him, Maul explained their options: either go with him or take their chances alone with the Inquisitor. In spite of their lowered voices, Maul heard their plan to flee once they reached his encampment, giving little amusement to their savior. As they descended a ladder into a lower corridor tunnel section, Maul took the opportunity to congratulate Izara on her fighting prowess against the Inquisitor, to which the Padawan attributed her master's teachings. When she asked about his master's betrayal, the Zabrak opened up about the pain Sidious had inflicted on him, thinking particularly of Savage. Izara followed up with whether the Sith lord was still alive, a question that stopped Maul in his tracks, and answered yes in defeated acknowledgement. Spybot then appeared and greeted its master warmly and closed behind the Padawan and police lieutenant's son.{{MSL|Chapter 7: Call to Oblivion}} Reaching his camp at the lowest level, Maul got informed by Kast of Imperial probes closing down on their location. Forced with the fact that Janix could no longer harbour their presence, Maul commanded for them to ready the ship and leave at once. As Kast explained their preparations, Maul sensed the departure of Izara and her friend Rylee to his annoyance. Fraught with impatience at the female Twilek undermining his proposed alliance at every turn, Maul jumped down to cut their escape on the landing platform, vocalising he was getting tired of Izara's decadence. When he was challenged that they could never take on the Empire, Maul rebutted the statement and told the young Jedi to join him, and he would divulge how they could topple the Emperor and his rule. Once again, not reaching through to her, the fugitive lost all forbearance of swaying with words and restrained the Padawan still with the Force while pushing away her companion. To his surprise, the young woman using the pure hatred of him managed to break free of his grip over her and ignited her lightsaber straight at Maul. He blocked with his own blade and fended her off, approaching her casually with his forces behind him. Just then, the sealed doors above hiding them opened, and Kast warned that their position to have been compromised.{{MSL|Chapter 7: Call to Oblivion}} Three Imperial LAAT [[gunship]]s descended upon them, filled with stormtroopers, and opened fire. Staring down at the face of Izara's defiance, Maul reluctantly turned his gaze to the superior numbers of Imeprials blasting at his limited soldiers and sparn in front to absorb most of the shots and deflect them back. To his surprise, he was eventually joined by Izara to kill their attackers until the Padawan tried to rescue the abducted Rylee. Continuing to swat away the incoming blaster bolts, Maul looked up at an elevated platform where Izara stood before she left, forcing Maul to keep fighting. After some time, he cut down the last of the stormtroopers and ordered them to reach their ship, knowing the Inquisitor to be inbound. Together, they departed from [[Sector Two-X]] and travelled through the tunnels to reach their hidden Mandalorian fighter.{{MSL|Chapter 7: Call to Oblivion}} [[File:TheCrowAndMarrokDuellingMaul.png|thumb|right|280px|After locating Maul, the First Brother and Eleventh Brother engaged Maul in an intense duel.]] While they escaped to their ship, [[Kebris]] and some of the Mandalorian commandos aired their grievances about the lost credits before Kast reminded them to stick to the mission. Believing perhaps it was time to remove any disloyal remnant soldiers, Kast debated her lord about the growing costs of his plan and feared his obsession with Izara had blinded Maul to the fact that the Padawan would never follow him. Refusing the idea that no bond could be severed, Maul reminded Kast to also bear that in mind. Finally reaching the bridge connecting a ravine, Maul and his forces could see their ship hidden behind a foss across the gap and sprinted towards with all haste. Unfortunately, Maul knew their pursuers to already be behind them and turned his lightsabers towards the stormtroopers behind them. Pushing through to reach the ship, they broke off and crossed a gate which the larger Zabrak brother pulled down, blocking them from the Imperials' pursuit. None of that mattered, however, as two more Imperial gunships cut off their escape route with two black cloaked figures jumping down.{{MSL|Chapter 7: Call to Oblivion}} One was the Inquisitor he had already fought, but the figure was now accompanied by a second member of the Jedi hunting organization. Frustrated to see himself and his followers trapped on all sides, the targeted Sith wasted no time in engaging the two Dark Side hunters, ordering his soldiers to fight off the Imperials and reach the ship. Taking his opponents away from the battlefield, Maul leapt away from the bridge to a catwalk tens of meters below. Though brokering the momentum of his fall with the Force, his previously fixed right leg broke at the knee joint due to the impact of his landing, faltering with electricity, much to Mauls pain. The two Inquisitors landed in front of him, and the three Dark Side users engaged in their duel again. Parrying a slash from the First Brother, Maul [[Force push]]ed away the second Inquisitor, the [[Eleventh Brother]], while throwing away his spinning double lightsaber at them. The First Brother jumped above, and the other Inquisitor lay on the floor and quickly recovered as Maul reclaimed his saber. The two Inquisitors jumped away to a larger platform, and Maul pursued. Fending off both opponents at once, Maul delivered a kick to the First Brother while keeping the Eleventh Brother at bay. When distracted by the First Brother, Maul got blasted with the Force by the Eleventh Brother and plunged his lightsaber down into the ground to stall his fall.{{MSL|Chapter 7: Call to Oblivion}} Seeing the open terrain unsuitable for two fighters, Maul saw a cave hidden by a waterfall and jumped into it and hid in the shadows. The Inquisitors chased him, but lost track of their target. Walking about through the cave, the Nightbrother capitalised on his greater ability at stealth and lured the First Brother away from the other Imperial to separate them. Now seeing the Eleventh Brother as vulnerable, Maul fell hard and suddenly upon the masked figure, only to surprisingly retreat from the relentless attacks of his competent foe. Managing to push him off with the Force, the Zabrak got swiftly kicked in the chest by the First Brother and recovered to meet him blade to blade. After a short exchange, Maul got knocked back again from a Force push by the First Brother and crashed into a stalactite with enough damage to break his already faulty leg to the point of kneeling. At that moment, the recovering Eleventh Brother saw the frailty of the Sith lord´s cybernetics. Wasting no time, the Inquisitor ran and swung at Maul, but he manoeuvred away from the blow. Growling in anger at the realisation that these two opponents together were starting to overwhelm him, Maul tried to distance himself from them. Forced to retreat as the two Inquisitors harmoniously covered each other's flanks, Maul had no time to finish off one foe before the other reengaged, cutting his Juyo offence off with their own aggressive style.{{MSL|Chapter 7: Call to Oblivion}} Holding both off in a lightsaber lock, Maul pressed them away. However, as he kept his attention on the First Brother, Maul unknowingly exposed his right leg, which was quickly bruised with the plasma blade of the Eleventh Brother, who capitalised on the crippling weakness. Crying out in pain from the scorched metal connected to his nervous system, Maul collapsed onto the rocky ground and tried to crawl away from his approaching killers. The Eleventh Brother spun his lightsaber in a quick 360-degree arch, prepared to deliver the final blow, but Maul was saved by the intervention of one of his fellow Dathomirian Nightbrother, [[Scorn]]. The Zabrak was quickly killed by the Inquisitor and disposed of, but despite being enraged by Scorn's death the distraction bought Maul enough time to retrieve his lightsaber and ready himself again for combat. Meanwhile outside Kebris and two commandos decided to abandon Maul but where killed when stealing the ''Hex''. Coldly approached by the two combatants, Maul saw a hole leading to a lower cave and jumped down. His barely functioning leg continues to buzz in resistance, and the relentless Inquisitors fell in front and behind Maul, forcing a new bout of swordplay. Now physically weakened, morally beaten, and mentally compromised, the ferocious Sith assassin barely delivered a strike before being kicked away by the First Brother.{{MSL|Chapter 7: Call to Oblivion}} Holding his hurt chest and standing on one knee, Maul knew he was in no shape to keep fighting the two of them. In spite of his superior skills with a double-bladed lightsaber and greater power in the Force, the last days had worn on his psyche, neutered the functionality of his right leg, and exposed him too early to the Empire. Clipping his lightsaber away, Maul raised his hands up, which the Inquisitors refused as a sign of surrender, stating they would fulfil the Emperor's command of killing him. Feigning whimpers, he then promised the same fate and pulled with all his might the Force on the cave around them, showing his surrender to be a ploy to bury them under a cave-in.{{MSL|Chapter 7: Call to Oblivion}} Pulling the entire environment down, Maul ran away as boulders fell and bounded out of the cave. Falling down, Maul ignited his lightsaber and started to spin around to drill through a catwalk below him and lost consciousness when hitting.{{MSL|Chapter 8: The Creeping Fear}} ====Fighting through his demons==== Tortured by the nightmares of his past, Maul awakens to find himself lying down with rocks around him. His face stares down on a puddle mirroring his visage. The reflection changes when a droplet ripples the image to his younger self, when he was still a boy of Dathomir. The unforeseen appearance irritates Maul, and he swats it away in hatred for his weaker self. Rising up in gruntled pain, he tries to brace himself on his damaged leg, but the damage to it has made its functionality limited. Limping towards a rubble of rocks, Maul tries to climb them, but his compromised leg gives in, and he stumbles down. Seeing a path forward and hearing the sounds of shuttles above, Maul grits his teeth and makes his way through the dark tunnel. Fighting his way through the long tunnel, a blistering wind of sand gusts against Maul, forcing him to hold his arms to see the way before him. Alone in the darkness of Janix, Maul's mind began to torture him with the sins of his past: the cackling of his master, the biting words of the First Brother, and a faint scream from his deceased brother. Trapped by the voices within his own head, Maul collapsed and screamed out for silence. [[File:MaulSavageSidious-MSL-Chapter8.png|thumb|left|280px|While escaping to meet up with his mercenaries, Maul saw some of his memories as Sidious' apprentice.]] The sand storm shrouding him then started to form faint shapes from his unreliable memories. First among them is the voice and appearance of a young Savage and Maul at the moment he was taken away from Dathomir. Maul is enraged when he sees Sidious luring the naive Maul away in spite of his older brother's pleas to stay. The next memory shows a sparring match between Maul and Palpatine, the evil Sith lord batting away Maul´s feeble swing and punishing his weakness with Force lightning. Maul covers his face to shield himself from all the mistakes of his youth, but is perturbed when seeing the moment he was cut in two by the Padawan Obi-Wan Kenobi. Third of the visions recovers his frantic descent into madness at Lotha Minor, grovelling at the abandonment of Darth Sidious. He then sees the moment he reunites with Savage, only to relive the horrifying image of Sidious plunging both lightsabers into his helpless brother while laughing with sadistic glee. The final vision shows the dying Savage as Maul holds his hand, proclaiming that his brother must not neglect to enact revenge against the Sith lord. Groaning and cringing in sorrow from the insurmountable pain of his past, Maul presses his hand in front of his eyes, denying to see the nightmares. When he looks back, all he sees is the sand blowing at him. Focusing on all his losses: his home, family and brother, the stubborn Dathomorian refused to bow down to these images and honing on his singular hatred for the one responsible for his deprived life: Sidious. Rising up and pushing through the sand blistering against his skin, Maul keeps pushing through despite his pain. Fueled by nothing but revenge, he manages to walk for hours through the seemingly endless tunnel and gets through the sandstorm, but is exhausted and limping by the point he reaches a smaller tunnel. Fully worn from the cascading walk and never-ending voices, the deliburoius Maul numbs from all the exerted effort and pats down onto the floor completely. Trying to get up, he once again looks upon the image of his younger self in a puddle, seeing the boy shudder and apologise meekly. Notwithstanding his usual hatred for cowardice, the defeated Maul treats the mirage with soft acceptance rather than furious refusal, quietly comforting his past self with the assurance that he will ''never'' allow the Emperor to commit the same vile acts on another individual. Closing his eyes to let the feelings sink in, the reflection changes when a tear drops from his own face warps the mirror into his current self; however, it now resembles a determined look of something other than vengeance. Picking himself up not for his own revenge against Sidious, but to ensure that he can spare others from his pain, Maul defiantly keeps on moving. Through sheer will and brandished grit, he reunites with his remaining forces and gets his leg fixed and patched. Taking refuge at the deceased Head Boss Deemis'office, Maul walks out to inspect the view over Janix City's surface and to contemplate in meditation.
