Gerrera believed Organa, like Mothma, to be tools of Palpatine ineffective at stopping him in the Senate and placated blame for the Clone Wars and the formation of the Empire on the Galactic Senate. Despite their differences, the two came to a unofficial alliance and understanding.<ref name="MOF3">''[[Reign of the Empire: The Mask of Fear]]''</ref> In later years, the pair could work together<ref name="Ghosts of Geonosis" /> but their relations deteriorated to the point where Organa believed him crazy.<ref name=":1">''[[Star Wars: Scum and Villainy: Case Files on the Galaxy's Most Notorious]]''</ref> Gerrera's dislike of Organa stemmed from when Organa covered his investigation, his involvement, and truth of the ordeal that took place in the [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Attack_on_Eyo-Dajuritz attack on Eyo-Dajuritz], and portrayed himself as a supporter of the Empire to curtail Imperial espionage by framing Gerrera as a aggressive Onderonian terrorist to push the [https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Imperial_Rebirth_Act Imperial Rebirth Act], with Gerrera genuinely willing to work with Organa. He also disliked how Organa previously treated "him as a threat" in their initial meeting when their loyalties became known.<ref name="MOF3" /> 

=====Mon Mothma=====
Mothma met Gerrera personally shortly after the formation of the Galactic Empire, having heard of him and seen images of him prior. Mothma initially found him clever, confident, charismatic, and pragmatic, surprised he was more concerned with public support than he would let on, and believed his strategies sector-wide conflicts but believed his strategies to be limiting. In turn, Gerrera saw her as a tool for Palpatine and ineffective in stopping him through the Senate. . Despite their differences, Gerrera and Mothma came to an understanding although they never openly contacted one other unless circumstances were dire.<ref name="MOF3" /> The pair would meet several times over the years, arguing over strategies for the rebel to take and the existence of a superweapon for hours in meetings. Their mutual relationship deteriorated over the years and he would come to regard her as weak and indecisive leader, though he did see fire in her, while Mothma regarded him as a war criminal and terrorist mired in cynicism.<ref name="Rebel Files3">''[[Star Wars: The Rebel Files]]''</ref>  

=====Alliance to Restore the Republic=====
{{Quote|I'm fighting for you and everyone else not to lose what they've got. And I won't apologize for how I do it.''"<br />"''Then you're no better than the Empire.|Saw Gerrera and Ezra Bridger|<ref name="Ghosts of Geonosis" />}}
 [[File:SawBailArgue-RogueOne2.png|right|thumb|270x270px|Saw Gerrera had a tenuous relationship with the other rebel cells.]]When Gerrera was first affiliated with the cell that eventually grew to be the Rebel Alliance, he and his Partisans had a reputation as effective soldiers and despite their tactics, they were initially welcomed.<ref name="Rebel Files3" /> This changed overtime, with Gerrera's view of them complex; some leaders criticized him for his lack of understanding people valuing peace more than freedom<ref name="Rebe Dossier2">''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: Rebel Dossier]]''</ref> and others believed he made it difficult for others to side with their efforts<ref name="Leia" /> and made him too comparable to the Empire.<ref name="Ghosts of Geonosis" /> In turn, Gerrera believed them frustrating for their focus on labels from the Empire, disliked how their leaders prioritized which missions to engage, others seeking him out for aid only for more controversial and less convenient missions,<ref name="Rebel Rising" /> found them cowardly for following the rules of engagement when the Empire does not,<ref name="In the Name of the Rebellion" /> and eventually believed they conspired to assassinate him for his past crimes and extremism.<ref name="Rogue One Visual Guide" /> However, despite his disillusionment, he supported their overall efforts, choosing to share his intel and urging his former protege Jyn to join and to save them.<ref name="Rogue One" /> 

==Skills and abilities==
===At all costs, even himself===
{{Quote|I will do whatever is required to be the victor.|Saw Gerrera, to Ezra Bridger|<ref name="In the Name of the Rebellion" />}}
[[File:Saw_Gerrera_SWDL.png|thumb|left|200px|While a popular leader, he also held a reputation for being a ruthless and effective Rebel commander.]]
During the Clone Wars, Gerrera was trained by the Jedi Order in the art of combat,<ref name="Saw Gerrera Databank" /> affording him abilities in reconnaissance, infiltration, leadership,<ref name="Join the Battle">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Character Encyclopedia - Join the Battle!]]''</ref> and knowledge in weaponry and military tactics.<ref name="A War on Two Fronts" /> By the Imperial era, he garnered a reputation as a effective soldier,<ref name="Saw Gerrera Databank" /> considered among the [[Galactic Empire's Most Wanted list|Galactic Empire's Most Wanted]] a feared insurgent who employed ghastly tactics<ref name="Rebel Files2">''[[Star Wars: The Rebel Files]]''</ref> and was ruthless, often taking no survivors.<ref name=":1">''[[Star Wars: Scum and Villainy: Case Files on the Galaxy's Most Notorious]]''</ref>

His abilities diminished overtime due to his failing health from a variety of factors: rhydonium fumes addiction,<ref name="I Have Friends Everywhere" /> adverse effects from barely hospitable hideouts,<ref name="Dawn VG" /> and a assassination attempt from [[teccitin]].<ref name="Guardians of the Whills" /> Beyond his habit of inhaling rhydonium,<ref name="TonyGilroy" /> he also sustained lung damage from Geonosian insecticides inhaled at near-lethal levels following a mission in Geonosis.<ref name="Rogue One Visual Guide" /> An injury to his legs forced him to use a prosthetic leg.<ref name="Rogue One" /> Jyn Erso was upset to see him reduced to a weakened state during their reunion on Jedha, mentally comparing him to the force of nature he had once appeared as.<ref name="Rogue One Junior Novel" />

===Military commander===
[[File:Saw-Gerrera-full-body-RORD.png|thumb|right|200px|Saw Gerrera toward the end of his life]]
A popular rebel leader,<ref name="Rogue One Visual Guide" /> both himself<ref name="Saw Gerrera Databank" /> and his rebel cell gained a reputation for their effectiveness in the battlefield despite their tactics.<ref name="Rebel Files" /> In his earlier years, he was once considered for a position of Governor for Onderon and noted for his ability to inspire others towards resistance, practicing speeches in order to help his agenda in recruitment. Mothma believed his agenda were suited for potential sector-wide success.<ref name="MOF" /> During his campaigns against the Empire, he had successful endeavors such as his victories in the [[Arkanis sector]], noted for being a rare display of anti-Empire ruthlessness from resistance movements and making things difficult for the Moff in charge of the sector.<ref name="Rebel Files2" />  

Gerrera was adept at assessing people and groups, a skill he taught to Jyn Erso after taking her in as his ward and protege.<ref name="Rebel Rising" /> Although paranoia impacted this later in his lifetime,<ref name="Rogue One" /> his assessments were often correct; his assessment of the Maya Pei Brigade was accurate,<ref name="Narkina 5" /> with the disappearance of their leader impacting them.<ref name="Sagrona Teema">{{Andor|Sagrona Teema}}</ref> He also predicted the existence of the Empire building a superweapon (the Death Star).<ref name="Rogue One" /><ref name="In the Name of the Rebellion" /> When investigating kyber crystals and the superweapon, the Empire was prompted to move it's location elsewhere due to how close Gerrera came to uncovering it.<ref name="Rogue One Visual Guide" /> Imperial Commander [[Kanchar]] noted Gerrera's efforts also captured a lot of kyber crystals from the Empire, admiring him for being competent his capabilities.<ref name="Star Wars 2015 39">[[Star Wars (2015) 39|''Star Wars'' (2015) 39]]</ref> He also uncovered spies within his ranks (both Imperial and Rebel alike)<ref name="Rebel Files" /><ref name="Rebel Rising" /><ref name="Ever Been to Ghorman?" /> and could using them for misdirection.<ref name="Ever Been to Ghorman?" />  

Despite his capabilities, Mothma and other rebel leaders in the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] believed his methods would often cause more problems for them, the former criticizing his actions often ostracized potential recruitment of powerful political candidates and believed him too pessimistic and underestimating of people's desire towards peace.<ref name="Rebel Files" /> [[Luthen Rael|Rael]] was also critical of his hesitance to near-inability to work alongside other rebel cells he didn't align with.<ref name="Narkina 5" /> His methods also collided with his own members at times, the [[Inusagi massacre|Inusagi mission]] in particular causing others to move towards other rebel cells.<ref name="Rebel Rising" />

===Combat abilities===
In combat, Gerrera was skilled in both armed and unarmed combat.<ref name="Join the Battle" /> His unarmed skills were formidable enough to overpower Ezra Bridger, Rex,<ref name="Ghosts of Geonosis" /> and incapacitate both [[stormtrooper]]s and [[death trooper]]s.<ref name="In the Name of the Rebellion" /> He could also use a variety of melee weaponry such as staves (in which he favored), truncheons, and knives in addition to ranged weaponry like a blaster, snipers, and explosives. He taught much of his combat skills to his protege, [[Jyn Erso]], who noted him to be rather quick and taught her to employ dirty tactics.<ref name="Rebel Rising" /> 

===Other skills===
Like other [[Onderonian outcasts]], Gerrera could also domesticate other animals such as a [[ruping]].<ref name="A War on Two Fronts" /> He was a trained pilot and experience in the Clone Wars also made him knowledgeable in various droid models and their weaknesses.<ref name="Rebel Rising" /> Gerrera was also an expert at interrogation and intimidation, employing ghastly techniques and unethical means to acquire information,<ref name="Rogue One Visual Guide" /> allowing him to gain intelligence and information more accurate than his Alliance counterparts despite being less well-equipped.<ref name="In the Name of the Rebellion" /> Conversely, he displayed resistance against interrogation and torture himself during the Clone Wars,<ref name="The Soft War Episode Guide" /> although this unintentionally hardened him into a remorseless warrior.<ref name="Rogue One Visual Guide" />

==Equipment==
Gerrera wielded multiple weapons; including an [[A140 blaster pistol]], a [[sniper rifle]],<ref name="Front Runners" /> and a [[DC-15A blaster carbine]].<ref name="The Soft War" /> Gerrera wore several different suits that acted as armor; he bore a [[Saw Gerrera's suit|pressurized suit]] sometime prior to his mission on Kashyyyk consisting of a [[plastoid]] ailette blackblast armor and a atmospheric sensor sampler and a Onderon banner he wore as a cape.<ref name="Rogue One Visual Guide" /><ref name="Jedi: Fallen Order" /> The suit would later also have a ventilator breaking tube.<ref name="Rogue One Visual Guide" /><ref name="Rogue One" /> He alternated with a lighter, green-colored [[Environment suit|vac-suit]] with a hermetic coupler, sealing wrist cuff, and corrugated articulation in the legs and arms.<ref name="Dawn VG" /> He often carried a [[DH-16 Blaster Pistol|DH-16 blaster pistol]] with a perforated cooling sleeve and also contained a grappling hook attachment within the weapon.<ref name="Dawn VG" /><ref name="Jedi: Fallen Order" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Development===
{{Quote|Saw Gerrera is maybe the original rebel. He is the first one in a long line of people that got trained by Jedi to fight for themselves; to save their planets during the Clone Wars. He's the beginning of what would eventually become the Rebel Alliance.|Dave Filoni, on Saw Gerrera|<ref name="YouTube The Original Rebel">{{SWYouTube|mLN_y-uWAVA|The Original Rebel: Saw Gerrera Returns | Star Wars Rebels|sw_url=video/disneyxd-saw-gerrera-returns-in-the-name-of-the-rebellion-preview-star-wars-rebels}}</ref>}}
[[File:SawGerrera-Masterwork2020.png|thumb|left|250px|Forest Whitaker as Saw Gerrera]]
The character of Saw Gerrera was voiced in the animated series ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]''<ref name="Kishino interview">{{SW|url=news/interview-andrew-kishino-saw-gerrera-on-the-clone-wars|text=Interview: Andrew Kishino - Saw Gerrera on ''The Clone Wars''}}</ref> and ''[[Star Wars: The Bad Batch]]'' by [[Andrew Kishino]].<ref name="TBBAftermath" /> Saw Gerrera was played by [[Forest Whitaker]] in the [[2016]] [[Star Wars Anthology Series|''Star Wars'' Anthology]] film ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'',<ref name="Rogue One" /> who returned to voice the character in ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]''<ref name="Ghosts of Geonosis" /> and the [[2019]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order]]''.<ref name="Jedi: Fallen Order" /> He was originally conceived by ''[[Star Wars]]'' creator [[George Lucas]] for the unproduced live-action television series ''[[Star Wars: Underworld]]''<ref name="New-R1">{{StarWarsShow|Filn82qphCA|New Rogue One Characters Revealed, LEGO Star Wars: The Freemaker Adventures|sw_url=video/the-star-wars-show-episode-7}}</ref> and Lucas later wanted to involve the character in an arc in the [[The Clone Wars: Season Five|fifth season]] of ''The Clone Wars'',<ref name="Filoni interview">{{SW|url=news/interview-dave-filoni-on-star-wars-the-clone-wars-season-five-part-1|text=Interview: Dave Filoni on ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' Season Five, Part 1}}</ref> where he first appeared in the episode "[[A War on Two Fronts]]",<ref name="A War on Two Fronts" /> which premiered on [[October 6]], [[2012]].<ref name="A War on Two Fronts EG old">{{SW|url=explore/the-clone-wars/ep502|text="A War on Two Fronts" - ''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide|nolive=1}}</ref>

''The Clone Wars'' and ''Rebels'' showrunner [[Dave Filoni]] described Gerrera as "the original rebel" because he was "the first one in a long line of people" who were trained by the Jedi during the Clone Wars as planetary defense insurgents. To Filoni, Gerrera is the beginning point for what eventually becomes the Rebel Alliance.<ref name="YouTube The Original Rebel" /> Accordingly, the character's name is a "mnemonic riff" on real-life [[Wikipedia:Argentinia|Argentinian]] revolutionary and associate of [[Wikipedia:Fidel Castro|Fidel Castro]] - [[Wikipedia:Che Guevara|Che Guevara]] as revealed in ''[[The Art of Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]''.<ref name="The Art of Rogue One">''[[The Art of Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]''</ref>

Andrew Kishino had been a huge ''[[Star Wars]]'' fan growing up. He had auditioned for the role as he thought that the character description had been a perfect fit of him. The script that had been sent out had been anomynized, with the character's names having been changed and the production name having been abreviated as "CW.", leading Kishino to think that it would be for a production of the television network [[Wikipedia:The CW|The CW]], and he only realized it when he turned up and saw Kenobi's voice actor [[James Arnold Taylor]]. The voice actors all recorded their lines together in a group.<ref name="Kishino interview" /> Kishino and Steela Gerrera's actor [[Dawn-Lyen Gardner]] had been friends already prior to working together on the series, but hadn't known that the other had been cast before meeting at the first session.<ref name="Steela interview">{{SW|url=news/interview-dawn-lyen-gardner-steela-gerrera-on-the-clone-wars|text=Interview: Dawn-Lyen Gardner — Steela Gerrera on ''The Clone Wars''}}</ref> Gerrera was modeled after the likeness of Kishino, and he his face was recorded for two of the four episodes and as such the character also shared some of his facial mannerisms. Kishino compared Gerrera's personality in the arc to that of a leader who is hard to everyone, but still cared for them like a big brother; comparing him to an [[Wikipedia:Alpha wolf|alpha wolf]] and his expirience with the subcultures of [[Wikipedia:Hip-hop|hip-hop]] and [[Wikipedia:New York|New York]]. Kishino had been thrilled and grateful when Filoni said that his character could end up as an action figure, due to him only having few ''Star Wars'' toys growing up in poor circumstances and his attatchment to them.<ref name="Kishino interview" />

[[Lucasfilm Story Group]]'s [[Kiri Hart]] was the one who suggested that the character be used in ''Rogue One''.<ref name="The Art of Rogue One" /> An inspiration for Gerrera's character in ''Rogue One'', according to [[Phil Szostak]], was [[Wikipedia:Colonel Kurtz|Colonel Kurtz]] from the novella ''[[Wikipedia:Heart of Darkness|Heart of Darkness]]'', adapted as [[Wikipedia:Francis Ford Coppola|Francis Ford Coppola's]] [[1979]] film [[Wikipedia:Apocalypse Now|''Apocalypse Now'']].<ref name="Talin In VII?">{{Twitter|PhilSzostak|status/943942175389138944|[[Phil Szostak]]|quote=Colonel Kurtz also served as inspiration for exiled rebel extremist Saw Gerrera in #RogueOne. The character is based on ivory trader Kurtz from Joseph Conrad's novella Heart of Darkness, one of my favorite books. #StarWars}}</ref> [[Pablo Hidalgo]] of the Lucasfilm Story Group also stated that Gerrera's origin in the Clone Wars<ref name="PabloCommentary1">{{Bluesky|infinata.bsky.social|post/3lotk4idfb22j|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|date=2025-05-10|quote=Wait’ll people find out what the Onderon arc of TCW that debuted Saw Gerrera was inspired by. 👀}}</ref> was inspired by the [[Wikipedia:Operation Cyclone|US government arming Mujahideen fighters in Afghanistan]] to battle the [[Wikipedia:USSR|USSR]], with Hidalgo specifically noting how Gerrera and his comrades were supplied with rocket launchers to take down enemy gunships.<ref name="PabloCommentary2">{{Bluesky|infinata.bsky.social|post/3lotknmu7os2j|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|date=2025-05-10|quote=The Republic covertly supplying rocket launchers to the freedom fighters to take out enemy gunships certainly seems familiar!}} {{C|In response to: "Wasn't there a direct parallel to the US government sending munitions to the Mujahideen?"}}</ref> According to writer [[Gary Whitta]], Forest Whitaker was the only actor they considered to play Gerrera in ''Rogue One''.<ref name="Only Forest">{{Twitter|garywhitta|status/1219451136572133377|[[Gary Whitta]]|quote=Yes. Forrest was always the only choice for Saw.}} {{C|in response to "''Did you have any actors in mind when writing Rogue One? And did any of these wishes get realised? (Doubt you'd tell us any of the actors you wished for but it didn't pan out?)''"}}</ref>

===''Andor'' return===
[[File:Andor_Saw_Gerrera_Poster.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Forest Whitaker as Saw Gerrera in his character poster]]
Whitaker reprised his role as Gerrera in the episodes "[[Narkina 5 (episode)|Narkina 5]]"<ref name="Narkina 5" /> and "[[Daughter of Ferrix]]" in the ''[[Star Wars: Andor]]'' television series.<ref name="Daughter of Ferrix" /> Executive producer and writer [[Tony Gilroy]] wanted Gerrera and the other legacy characters to not provide fan service.<ref name="Real People">{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2022/tv/news/star-wars-andor-tony-gilroy-diego-luna-1235348148|text=How ‘Andor' Became the First ‘Star Wars' TV Series for Grown-Ups: ‘I Wanted to Do It About Real People'|author=Vary, Adam B|archivedate=20220824140042}}</ref> The night before a rehearsal for Gerrera and Luthen Rael's argument in "Narkina 5," Whitaker asked director [[Toby Haynes]] questions about backstory and kyber crystals. During the rehearsal, Whitaker and Rael's actor, [[Stellan Skarsgård]], read the scene for the first time and went at each other. According to Haynes, when the scene was filmed for real, Whitaker and Skarsgård almost deconstructed what they did in a natural and spontaneous way. They then had to completely reconstruct the scene, and it was hard to get to the same pitch. Haynes wanted to end Gerrera's rant with a very direct, face-on shot of Whitaker to build the intensity and bring the audience into the argument. To accomplish this, Haynes had Whitaker do his speech several times, telling him to "go crazy with it."<ref name="Career Highlight">{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-features/andor-episode-8-toby-haynes-forest-whitaker-stellan-skarsgard-1235250954|text=‘Andor' Director Toby Haynes Talks That Forest Whitaker-Stellan Skarsgard Scene: “It Was a Career Highlight”|author=Davids, Brian|date=2022-10-28|archivedate=20221029050743}}</ref>

According to Gilroy, at the time of ''Rogue One'', the crew did not have an answer to what Gerrera was inhaling through his breathing mask. However, for Gerrera's return in [[Andor Season 2|''Andor'' Season 2]], writer [[Beau Willimon]] proposed to Gilroy that Gerrera was inhaling rhydonium fuel fumes, which Gilroy liked. According to Gilroy, Luthen Rael giving Gerrera the ability to steal fuel was a gift that firmed up their bond forever. Gerrera's speech about rhydonium<ref name="RhydoHigh">{{WebCite|url=https://ew.com/andor-creator-tony-gilroy-explains-saw-gerrera-mask-sucking-origin-story-11723317|text=Andor creator Tony Gilroy explains Saw Gerrera mask-sucking origin story|author=Ross, Dalton|date=2025-05-02|archivedate=20250503021646}}</ref> in the episode "[[I Have Friends Everywhere]]"<ref name="I Have Friends Everywhere" /> was written by Willimon, with Gilroy then doing a first pass on the speech and loving what was put down.<ref name="RhydoHigh" /> While the [[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story (novelization)|''Rogue One'' novelization]] by [[Alexander Freed]]<ref name="R1Novel" /> and [[Star Wars: Rogue One: A Junior Novel|junior novelization]] by [[Matt Forbeck]] had previously suggested Gerrera was inhaling oxygen by identifying Gerrera's breathing mask as an oxygen mask,<ref name="Rogue One Junior Novel" /> [[StarWars.com]] confirmed that Gerrera had been inhaling rhydonium through his<ref name="TonyGilroy" /> oxygen mask<ref name="Rogue One Junior Novel" /> during the events of ''Rogue One''.<ref name="TonyGilroy" />

===Concept art===
[[File:Bizarre_Saw_Gerrera_concept_art.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Early conceptual art for Saw Gerrera's live-action appearance in ''Rogue One'' by Aaron McBride inspired by Colnel Kurtz]]
Character illustration concept art of Gerrera for ''The Clone Wars'' was done by [[Tara Rueping]]<ref name="A War on Two Fronts EG" /> and a character illustration of him with a cloak for the "[[The Soft War]]" was done by [[Will Nichols]] and [[Carlos Sanchez]].<ref name="The Soft War Episode Guide" /> and finished on [[January 19]], [[2011]].<ref name="10 things">{{SW|url=news/10-things-you-should-know-about-saw-gerrera-from-the-clone-wars|text=10 Things You Should Know About Saw Gerrera from ''The Clone Wars''}}</ref>

For ''Rogue One'' concept art of the character was done by multiple artists: [[Aaron McBride]] designed a piece with Gerrera on a "throne" in a jungle with a pile of Imperial helmets on the ground<ref name="The Art of Rogue One" /> in [[2014]]. The piece, inspired by Colnel Kurtz,<ref name="ArtStation McBride">{{ArtStation|username=aaronmcbride|url=artwork/1rwx8|name=Aaron McBride|text=Saw Gerrera sitting on Throne Concept . Rogue One: A Star Wars Story ( 2016 )|quote=Ha. Yeah this was back in 2014. I tried making him a little more "Col. Kurtz" back then.}}</ref> depicted him white skin and robotic right arm and legs and had a scarred face missing his left eye. [[Adam Brockbank]] also produced a piece with him in a yellow suit with breathing tubes, while Brockbank and [[Glyn Dillon]] designed multiple pieces of his final design. Other pieces featuring him were also done by [[Thom Tenery]], [[Erik Tiemens]], [[Will Htay]]<ref name="The Art of Rogue One" /> and [[Vincent Jenkins]].<ref name="Vincent Jenkins">{{Twitter|vincentj_artist|status/1985360297968975972|[[Vincent Jenkins]]|date=2025-11-03|quote="Rogue One" early idea for Saw Gerrera. #StarWars}}</ref> Gerrera's updated model for ''Rebels'' was designed as a middle ground between his different looks in ''The Clone Wars'' and ''Rogue One'' and was designed by [[Kilian Plunkett]].<ref name="ArtoRebels">''[[The Art of Star Wars Rebels]]''</ref> Gerrera's model for ''The Bad Batch'' was finished by [[Jason Pichon]] on [[April 19]], 2019.<ref name="Aftermath EG">{{SW|url=series/the-bad-batch/aftermath-episode-guide|text="Aftermath" Episode Guide | The Bad Batch}}</ref> Concept art of Gerrera's costume for ''Andor'' was done by costume designer [[Michael Wilkinson]].<ref name="AndorCostumeConcept">{{Instagram|username=michaelwilkinson|url=p/DNTRW-BRRp6|name=[[Michael Wilkinson]]|date=2025-08-14|quote=I wanted to share more details of mighty #SawGerrara , played by the wonderful @forestwhitaker - in #Andor, we portrayed Saw 5 years before #RogueOne - a bit younger, and not yet completely weighed down by his addictions and obsessions. Shown in this post too are some of his militia - a motley crew of humans and creatures! #costumes #costumedesign #starwars #fyc}}</ref>

===Contradictions===
The [[2026]] comic [[Rogue One – Saw Gerrera 1|''Rogue One – Saw Gerrera'' 1]] depicts a version of Gerrera rescuing the Erso family from Coruscant during All-Species Week,<ref name="SawGerrera1" /> although it differs heavily from the event as it was originally depicted in the [[2016]] novel ''[[Catalyst: A Rogue One Novel]]''. While ''Catalyst'' depicts Gerrera as approaching the Erso family in a crowded spaceport before they withdraw to his ship,<ref name="Catalyst" /> ''Rogue One – Saw Gerrera'' 1 depicts Gerrera as landing in front of the Ersos aboard a YV-865 ''Aurore''-class freighter and calling out that they need to leave right then for the fireworks to give them cover. Gerrera identifies the Erso family before kneeling down to speak with Jyn, whom he asks to be brave like her father.<ref name="SawGerrera1" /> This article sides with the novel's version of events.

Despite only being set in 17 BBY, the art within ''Rogue One – Saw Gerrera'' 1 makes Gerrera resemble how as he appears<ref name="SawGerrera1" /> in ''Jedi: Fallen Order''<ref name="Jedi: Fallen Order" /> and the flashbacks of ''Rogue One: A Star Wars Story'',<ref name="Rogue One" /> which occur in 14 BBY and 13 BBY, respectively.<ref name="Timelines" /> However, his description in ''Catalyst'' during the same time period<ref name="Catalyst" /> as the comic<ref name="SawGerrera1" /> describes Gerrera to resemble his appearance from ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars''.<ref name="A War on Two Fronts" /> Indeed, Gerrera is depicted much like his ''The Clone Wars''-appearance in ''[[Star Wars: The Bad Batch]]'',<ref name="The Summit" /> which features Gerrera in 19 BBY<ref name="Timelines" /> and during or after 18 BBY.<ref name="TBB Date" /> As such, this article assumes that Gerrera's depiction in ''Rogue One – Saw Gerrera'' 1 is simply an act of artistic license.
